## A flight over the Nazca Lines: what can you see from the aircraft?

The [Nazca Lines](/peru/place/nazca-lines-and-ballestas-islands/) lie in the dry coastal desert of southern Peru. Ancient people created enormous images of animals, birds and plants, along with geometric figures. From the ground, many drawings look like separate strips and furrows. Only from a height is it easy to understand how the lines form complete figures.

Our excursion includes **35 minutes in a small aircraft**. Landmarks on the route include the monkey, hummingbird, spider and human figures, as well as geometric patterns. This is the advertised flight duration itself: travel to the airfield, check-in and time spent waiting for departure must be counted separately.

## Why the geoglyphs survived in the desert

According to UNESCO's World Heritage Centre, the Nazca and Palpa designs were created during different periods of pre-Columbian history, including approximately the fifth century BCE to the fifth century CE. Ancient artists removed darker stones from the surface to expose lighter soil underneath. The resulting contrast, together with an exceptionally dry climate, helped preserve the figures.

In 1994, the Nazca and Palpa Lines and Geoglyphs were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. Researchers study the designs in relation to the religious and social life of ancient cultures. Several explanations of their purpose exist, so it would be misleading to present any single hypothesis as a proven answer.

Two main types of ground drawings occur here: recognizable silhouettes of living creatures, and long straight lines, trapezoids, spirals and other geometric forms. During the flight, shift your gaze between individual figures and the surrounding desert pattern.

## How the scenic flight works

During our excursion, you fly over the desert in a small aircraft and return to the airfield after a 35-minute flight. The route allows views of several well-known geoglyphs, but the order in which particular figures are shown and the conditions for photography depend on the agreed flight program and crew instructions.

The aircraft may turn to give passengers a view of the lines. This matters if you are prone to motion sickness. Prepare your camera in advance and follow the crew's rules regarding seat belts and the use of devices during the flight.

Confirm the exact airfield, actual departure time, luggage restrictions and boarding requirements when arranging the excursion. Weather and operational restrictions may affect the flight. A fixed schedule cannot be promised for every date.

## Nazca Lines and the Paracas Candelabra: what is the difference?

The Andean Candelabra is on an arid coastal slope near Paracas and can be seen from the sea. The Nazca Lines form a much larger set of geoglyphs in the inland desert, viewed in part from an aircraft. They are different archaeological sites in different locations.

On our combined itinerary, the flight comes after exploring the coast and islands. The marine section is also available separately on the [Paracas and Ballestas Islands excursion](/peru/paracas/paracas-ballestas-islands-tour/). When choosing a combined day, consider not only the flight time but also ground transfers, possible waiting time and the return to your overnight accommodation.

## Preparing for the flight

Light clothing, a small bag and a camera with a securely fastened strap are convenient for a short scenic flight. The desert sun can be strong, but choose clothes with both the temperature at the airport and conditions in the cabin in mind.

If you have a medical condition that requires an assessment before flying or sharp maneuvers, discuss it with a doctor ahead of time. If you are prone to motion sickness, notify the organizer early rather than waiting until boarding. The specific air operator determines admission and restrictions.

Do not walk onto the geoglyphs in search of a close-up photograph: their preservation depends on protecting the desert surface. For a wider choice of Peruvian archaeological attractions, compare [excursions throughout Peru](/peru/excursion/) and culture-focused programs in the [Culture and History section](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Nazca flight

### How long is the flight?

The current Ada Tours description specifies **35 minutes**. Ground transfers, airport formalities and waiting time are not included in that figure.

### Can you see every geoglyph on one flight?

The itinerary describes several famous figures, but the archaeological area is far larger than any one scenic route. The particular flight program and visibility depend on operations and weather.

### How does the flight differ from a boat excursion at Paracas?

The aircraft shows the Nazca Desert drawings from above. A boat off [Paracas](/peru/place/paracas/) visits the Candelabra and marine islands, where travelers observe animals and birds.

### Is the excursion suitable for travelers prone to motion sickness?

Small-aircraft flights involving viewing turns can be uncomfortable. Discuss suitable preparation individually with a doctor and inform the organizer of any relevant health considerations before arranging the trip.
